results.q: What happens when a monitored node's heartbeat times out?
answer: Losing the data is detected in CO_SDOserver_process() (301/CO_SDOserver.c:1072), which checks `ret == CO_SDO_RT_waitingResponse`.

results.q: Where is the NMT operating state set?
answer: It is set in CO_NMT_getInternalState():
CO_NMT_getInternalState() (301/CO_NMT_Heartbeat.h:248) — Query current NMT state.
Step by step, it checks `(NMT == NULL)` (line 250); if true it returns `(NMT == NULL) ? CO_NMT_INITIALIZING : NMT->operatingState` straight away.
The result is stored in CO_process.NMTstate by CO_process() (CANopen.c:1314: `CO_NMT_internalState_t NMTstate = CO_NMT_getInternalState(co->NMT)`).
The result is stored in CO_process_SYNC.NMTstate by CO_process_SYNC() (CANopen.c:1412: `CO_NMT_internalState_t NMTstate = CO_NMT_getInternalState(co->NMT)`).
The result is stored in CO_process_RPDO.NMTisOperational by CO_process_RPDO() (CANopen.c:1441: `bool_t NMTisOperational = CO_NMT_getInternalState(co->NMT) == CO_NMT_OPERATIONAL`).
The result is stored in CO_process_TPDO.NMTisOperational by CO_process_TPDO() (CANopen.c:1474: `bool_t NMTisOperational = CO_NMT_getInternalState(co->NMT) == CO_NMT_OPERATIONAL`).

Related values are also set here: `NMT->operatingState = CO_NMT_INITIALIZING` in CO_NMT_init() (301/CO_NMT_Heartbeat.c:95); `NMT->operatingStatePrev = CO_NMT_INITIALIZING` in CO_NMT_init() (301/CO_NMT_Heartbeat.c:96); `NMT->operatingState = NMTstateCpy` in CO_NMT_process() (301/CO_NMT_Heartbeat.c:264); `NMT->operatingStatePrev = NMTstateCpy` in CO_NMT_process() (301/CO_NMT_Heartbeat.c:205); `SDO->state = CO_SDO_ST_IDLE` in CO_SDOserver_init() (301/CO_SDOserver.c:271); `LSSslave->lssState = CO_LSS_STATE_WAITING` in CO_LSSslave_init() (305/CO_LSSslave.c:200).

answer: This is handled in CO_SDOserver_init_canRxTx() (301/CO_SDOserver.c:151): it checks `(COB_IDClientToServer == SDO->COB_IDClientToServer) && (COB_IDServerToClient == SDO->COB_IDServerToClient)`, and when that is true it returns `CO_ERROR_NO`, so the rest of CO_SDOserver_init_canRxTx() is skipped.

results.q: What does CO_fifo_write do when the fifo is full?
answer: There is no `CO_fifo_write` in this code (none of its 2444 indexed symbols has that name). The closest names are CO_EM_t.fifoCount (301/CO_Emergency.h:278), CO_FIFO_H (301/CO_fifo.h:22), CO_CONFIG_FIFO (301/CO_fifo.h:28), described below.

CO_EM_t.fifo is a field of type `CO_EM_fifo_t *`, defined in 301/CO_Emergency.h:267 — the code describes it as: "Internal circular FIFO buffer for storing pre-processed emergency messages. Messages are added by CO_error() function. All messages are later post-processed by CO_EM_process() function. In case of overflow, error is indicated but emergency message is not sent. Fifo is also used for error history, OD object 0x1003, "Pre-defined error field". Buffer is defined by CO_EM_init().".

It is set by CO_EM_init() (`em->fifo = fifo`, line 358); CO_EM_process() (`em->fifo[fifoPpPtr].msg |= (uint32_t)errorRegister << 16`, line 578); CO_error() (`em->fifo[fifoWrPtr].msg = errMsg`, line 698); CO_error() (`em->fifo[fifoWrPtr].info = infoCodeSwapped`, line 700).
It is read by OD_read_1003() (line 185), CO_EM_process() (line 578).

In short: CO_EM_t.fifo carries a value produced by CO_EM_init(), CO_EM_process(), CO_error() and consumed by CO_EM_process(), OD_read_1003(). CO_EM_process() both reads and updates it, so it also keeps state between calls.
CO_CANrx_t.CANrx_callback is a field of type `void (*)(void *, void *)`, defined in example/CO_driver_target.h:62.
It is set by CO_CANmodule_init() (`rxArray[i].CANrx_callback = NULL`, line 65); CO_CANrxBufferInit() (`buffer->CANrx_callback = CANrx_callback`, line 110).
It is read by CO_CANinterrupt() (line 309).

CO_CANrx_t.CANrx_callback holds a function: at run time it points to CO_HBcons_receive(), CO_LSSslave_receive(), CO_NMT_receive(), CO_PDO_receive(), CO_SDO_receive(), CO_SYNC_receive(), CO_TIME_receive() (registered at 301/CO_NMT_Heartbeat.c:129, 301/CO_HBconsumer.c:213, 301/CO_PDO.c:560, 301/CO_PDO.c:682, 301/CO_SYNC.c:101, 301/CO_SYNC.c:285, 301/CO_SDOserver.c:171, 301/CO_TIME.c:125, 305/CO_LSSslave.c:209); it is called by CO_CANinterrupt().
In short: CO_CANrx_t.CANrx_callback carries a value produced by CO_CANmodule_init(), CO_CANrxBufferInit() and consumed by CO_CANinterrupt().
